alex: Heads up — PR #3301 (prefetching guide + SDK examples) is blocked. Reviewer asked for runtime confirmation about Cache-Control semantics and what happens on stream aborts. Also docs-preview linkcheck failed on an external model-card URL. Tagging @luke and @emily for runtime/SDK behavior.

priya: Which line in the guide needs clarification? I tried to be explicit but reviewer said the phrasing around caching + streaming is too hand-wavy. Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3301

alex: The paragraph that says "prefetch caching respects response headers" — reviewer wants exact behavior for `Cache-Control: no-store` vs `no-cache`, and whether client aborts can leave entries in the KV/prefix cache. Also the JS streaming snippet uses `controller.abort()` in the example; reviewer wants to know whether that can cause partial cache writes.

ci-bot: docs-preview job #540 failed: linkcheck error - external host modelcards.example.org returned 403. Logs: /builds/3301/logs/540

luke: Quick runtime note: server-side prefix/KV caching honors `Cache-Control` directives for public/shared cache. Behavior summary: `no-store` = do not write to cache; `no-cache` = allow storing but require revalidation on read. For internal prefix cache (our optimized token prefix store) we treat `no-cache` as "store but tag for revalidation" — it will still reduce cost but may trigger a revalidation path on subsequent requests. Regarding client aborts: currently if a stream is aborted mid-response, the server will not finalize/flush the cache entry. We only write when the response completes successfully. So partial aborts should not leave valid cache entries.

emily: SDK note: JS + Python SDKs do not set any `Cache-Control` header by default. Users must opt-in via request metadata or helper options. The streaming abort currently sends an application-level abort signal; SDK does not set any extra header to instruct runtime to drop or persist. We're planning a small runtime+SDK improvement to send an `x-cache-write` header for explicit cache writes, but that's post-ship. For doc wording: 1) call out that `no-store` will prevent cache writes, 2) if you abort a stream the server won't finalize cache entries (so safe), 3) show how to set `headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' }` in the example.

priya: Great, that covers the questions. I'll add a short table-like note: "Cache-Control behavior: no-store = no write; no-cache = stored but revalidated; default = stored." Keep it short. Also I'll replace the external model-card link with an internal mirror for the preview to avoid the linkcheck flake.

alex: Can we get a runtime + SDK approval so we can merge during the 2pm window?

luke: I'll +1 after the PR swaps the external link and adds the explicit header example. Confirmed: server behavior is as above — no finalization on aborted streams.

emily: I'll +1 once the snippet shows how to set headers. Example snippet to include in the PR: ```js
// ensure request is not cached by runtime
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'rwd-ggml-1.0',
  input: 'summarize this',
  headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' }
})
// streaming abort example
const controller = new AbortController()
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)
await client.stream({ ... }, { signal: controller.signal })
```
